\begin{CRchronicle}{99}
Those three days of Ash went the way the dark month goes when nobody draws a boundary across it — one ordinary tending day, one Account-day, one ordinary tending day, each lived and none spent to make a lesson of another. On the nineteenth and again on the twenty-first Sella Vail went to the hearth before the basket, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot and said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would have said I. She went wide around seven walked-around places with a look and no number, turned the dressed grain once under wool without a handful, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire and left the hairline showing, and set the rim two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. At the well Ilva answered \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, hand to sleeve and the notched wood unread. Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, and stopped the ear-sentence short of the calling word. Jorra spoke to the wheel before any person and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of a sentence unfinished.

On the twentieth the dark month’s second Account-day came to the Cross, earned by its own morning. Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and the sweet green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, and under the hot clay of him the smell of nothing at all. He wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket, called the levy and denied it — \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me}, \emph{your house}, never I — and went off up the road with the box locked and Ash’s second subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The bell went four, four and a gap and nobody crossed himself. Eight arithmetics of the year now stand behind one printed figure, eight and not one account; the figure read is still not the figure paid, and no hand writes between the two.

Each night the hand outside the wool went up an inch, took a small intake, held it whole on the river’s finishing and came straight down — answers 271 through 276, exact and worth nothing at two inches of air. Two hundred and seventy-six honest answers stood on the sixth place, each an object and not a power. Three hundred and fifty days stood exact and spoken by nobody; the carried fire kept four pulls and a gap, the boards four nails, four and a thumb-width knot, and nothing under that roof was opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended. What the three days cost was attention, which no institution can tax, and the keeping of a number nobody speaks.
\end{CRchronicle}
